title: Abigail (1 Samuel 25)
hookLine: a wise woman stops David's rage with food and words
last: I WILL NOT PUT FORTH MY HAND.

cards: "Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse?" That's the answer David's young men bring back. They had gone politely to a rich sheep owner named Nabal at shearing time, a time of feasting.
David's band had camped near Nabal's shepherds in the wilderness and kept them safe; now they asked for whatever he could spare. Nabal sends them off with an insult.
David says one thing to his men: gird on your swords, and he buckles on his own. By the time a servant runs to tell Nabal's wife, David is already on the road, and he's not coming to talk.

teach.b: The servant tells Abigail everything. The text calls her a woman of good understanding, and her husband churlish. She doesn't wait, and she doesn't tell Nabal.

She loads donkeys with bread and wine, meat and grain, raisins and figs, and rides out. She meets David coming down a mountain path. He has already sworn that by morning no male of Nabal's house will be left.

Abigail gets off her donkey, falls at his feet, and says: upon me, my lord, let the blame be. Each step of her speech counts. She doesn't defend her husband; his name means fool, she says, and folly is with him.
She takes the fault on herself. Then she looks past today. When God has made you ruler over Israel, you won't want this on your heart: blood shed for nothing, saving yourself with your own hand.

teach.h: PICTURE WHO YOU'LL WANT TO BE.
teach.b: She gives an angry man a picture of who he'll want to have been. And David stops.
Blessed be the Lord who sent you to meet me, he says, "and blessed be thy discretion," and blessed be you, who kept me from bloodguilt.

The Hebrew for discretion is ta'am, which also means taste: the sense to tell what fits the moment. Not a soldier, not one of his own men: a woman with food and the right words turned him from rage to blessing.
The rabbis of the Talmud remember her among the women of Israel they count as prophets.

how: Jews read Abigail's story in the book of Samuel, part of the Prophets, and the Talmud remembers her among the women it counts as prophets.

o: the woman whose wise words turned David from bloodshed
the wife who warned David that Saul was coming
the shepherd's wife who hid David from Nabal

s: Abigail asked her husband before she rode out
the text says she didn't tell Nabal. she loaded the donkeys and went.
Abigail took the blame onto herself
she fell at David's feet and said, upon me, my lord, let the blame be.
David stayed angry with Abigail for stopping him
he blessed God for sending her, blessed her discretion, and blessed her.

games.q: you're Abigail. your husband has insulted a man with an armed band, and they're on the road toward your house. what do you do?
o: warn your husband and let him handle it.
ride out with food and meet David yourself.
run with the servants into the hills.
games.why: she loads donkeys with bread, wine, meat and fruit, rides out without telling Nabal, and talks David out of bloodshed.

practice: Let someone come to mind who's angry right now, or often is. Abigail did three things: she came with something in her hands, she took some of the weight on herself, and she pointed past the anger to who he'd want to be.
Choose the one that fits your person, and hold it.

wordCard.voice: Abigail. The woman of good understanding who rode out with bread and wine, met David's rage on a mountain path, and turned it. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: your discretion, from ta'am, taste or judgment, in 1 Samuel 25:33.

carryVoice: Your line: blessed be thy discretion. The right words, at the right moment. See you tomorrow.
